clue.text: Author taking plant round close to troughs for animal

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright and wit

indicators.note: the plant goes round, enclosing the following letter

parts.note: beet is a root-vegetable plant

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A writer carries a plant around the end of the feeding troughs to give to some beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the S (last letter of 'troughs') inside BEET, making BESET.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu of the African plains is a large antelope, an animal.

definitions.meaning: a light curse uttered in annoyance

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a casual intensifier and also as a gentle expletive.

parts.note: stale means old, no longer fresh
mates are friends

explanation.surface: Someone keeps neckwear that once belonged to former pals.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a draw by having no legal move is a tie, so these are drawn games.

clue.text: 13 holds Cluedo's Green up in the "Green Man", perhaps

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: the answer to 13 across is a colour, and tan is a shade of it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Reverend Green is a suspect in the board game Cluedo, giving the abbreviation Rev

explanation.surface: A green-themed pub somehow features the board-game character Green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the clergyman's title, read upwards in a down clue. The Green Man is a common English pub name, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Man is a typical pub name, so it exemplifies an inn or public house.

clue.text: Then become a member of unworkable panels?

definitions.text: Then become a member of unworkable panels?

parts.words: Then become a member of unworkable panels?
parts.note: panels that cannot be panel-beaten are unworkable: the proverb about yielding to an unbeatable opponent

explanation.surface: Advice to someone faced with panels that cannot be worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: A panel beater hammers out car body panels; panels you cannot beat are 'unworkable'. Joining them is becoming a member.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb advises joining a side you cannot defeat, read here literally about panel beating.

indicators.note: the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: heaven is paradise

explanation.surface: Something is great, but falls a little short of perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' removes the last letter N from HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to rise and swell, as a sea or a chest does.

clue.text: Offence taken at failure to have good time

parts.note: a dud is a failure
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone is offended at being unable to enjoy themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To take dudgeon is to take offence, a state of indignant resentment.

clue.text: Radiant queen's back inside palace of archbishop, not having reached conclusion

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the shortened palace name
the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: Lambeth Palace is the London residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A glowing queen returns to the archbishop's palace before the matter is concluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having reached conclusion' trims LAMBETH to LAMBET; 'queen's back' is N, which goes inside. 'back' looks like a reversal but picks the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that glows or flickers softly, so it means radiant.

clue.text: Colour in which one's knitted cardigan, finally

parts.note: you knit your brow when frowning

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A colour used in knitting a cardigan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' suggests wool and the cardigan, but one knits one's brow when frowning.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common colour, the shade of earth or wood.

clue.text: One satirising plan more ludicrously, with nothing in it

indicators.note: the zero goes in the jumbled letters
ludicrously means absurdly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A satirist works out a plan, even more absurdly, with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ludicrously' rearranges PLANMORE into LAMPONER; 'in it' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes lampoons is a satirist, mocking targets in verse or prose.

clue.text: Interrupting rest, boy beginning to get up for work in harbour

indicators.note: the reversed letters break into the word for rest

parts.note: to lie is to rest

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Gareth is a boy's name

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lad breaks off his nap to get up and go to work at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lighters are flat-bottomed barges that ferry cargo between ships and quay; 'up' reverses the boy and the G together because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighterage is the work of moving cargo on lighters, barges in a harbour.

clue.text: On cloud nine, Spooner's got a stash of grass?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the first sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: a hiding is a hidden store, a stash
rye is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A euphoric person has a secret store of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of HIDING RYE to get the sound of RIDING HIGH. 'grass' also suggests marijuana, explaining the cloud nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding high means doing well and feeling elated, the same as being on cloud nine.

clue.text: Newspaper unwavering in viewpoint — pull back about it

parts.note: even means steady, unwavering

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about the viewpoint
back means the word is read the other way

parts.note: to drag is to pull
a stand is a position or viewpoint

explanation.surface: A paper is consistent in its opinion and urged to retract it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAG into GARD, which goes 'about' STAND to make GSTANDARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Evening Standard is a London newspaper.

definitions.meaning: a list of ideas is what an inventor might jot down

explanation.definitionFit: Visionary describes someone guided by lofty ideals; split, the word becomes a list of ideas.

clue.text: Compiler taken back, inspired by study on new European city, which some swear by

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so it goes inside
new signals the letters are made anew, rearranged
the word is read backwards

parts.note: a compiler of crosswords is a setter
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, retreating to a study in a new European city, swears by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for 'study on', not part of 'new European city'; the city is simply Rome. Tourette's can cause involuntary swearing, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This neurological condition can cause involuntary swearing, so some sufferers swear because of it.

clue.text: Having removed bottom and top, relatives appear so?

definitions.text: Having removed bottom and top, relatives appear so?

indicators.note: the last letter of the first relative is taken off

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: the first letter of the second relative is taken off

parts.note: a dad is a relative

explanation.surface: Family members who have stripped off their trousers and shirts look naked.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLE loses its bottom to give UNCL, DAD loses its top to give AD. Read as a whole, relatives stripped of bottoms and tops are naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means naked, as anyone with clothes off top and bottom would be.

parts.note: a cap is a lid
on as in fixed in place, secured

explanation.surface: With the lid fastened, the bird is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' suggests cooked, but a capon is a castrated cockerel: 'done' as in neutered.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a cockerel that has been castrated, so a bird that has been done.

clue.text: Irritable, having run into professional driver

indicators.note: the run goes into the driver

parts.note: a cabby drives a taxi for a living
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy after being hit by a taxi driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means bad-tempered and irritable.

clue.text: Lover originally having broken heart, what's so amusing?

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the heart word

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A heartbroken lover wonders what there is to laugh about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like an anagram, but L breaks into TICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickler is something that tickles, amusing a person.

definitions.meaning: to stop the flow of something, such as blood

explanation.definitionFit: Staunching stems a loss of blood, and a staunch supporter is firm and loyal.

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a drug is really snorted, and is told it isn't.
explanation.definitionFit: A soup tureen is a large lidded serving pot.

parts.note: vans are a form of transport

explanation.surface: English vehicles are provided for a man from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Evans is a typical Welsh surname, standing for a man of Wales.

parts.note: a moaning ailment, with the second part read as an organ in the body and the book section a reader is referred to

explanation.surface: A moaning grievance is being passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: This medical complaint is a recurring mild inflammation; 'whingeing' gives the adjective and 'referred to' hints at a book's back section.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a mild, recurring inflammation of the bowel organ.
